authors: and others (Meta AI; about 60 authors listed)

question: Can a single model translate speech and text between up to 100 languages across S2ST, S2TT, T2ST, T2TT and ASR, and match or beat cascaded systems?
hypothesis: A direct multitask model built on self-supervised speech pre-training, a multilingual NLLB text model and mined speech alignments can close the gap with strong cascaded systems.
contributions: SeamlessAlign: about 470,000 hours of automatically aligned speech translation data, built with an extended LID model and the Sonar multimodal embedding space
w2v-BERT 2.0 speech pre-training on 1 million hours
SeamlessM4T-Large (2.3B) and Medium (1.2B): one multitask UnitY model for S2ST, S2TT, T2ST, T2TT and ASR
Robustness benchmarks (noisy Fleurs, speaker variation), added-toxicity (ASR-ETOX) and gender-bias evaluation
Open release of models, inference code, fine-tuning recipes (Fairseq2) and SeamlessAlign metadata

method.summary: A three-stage fine-tuned multitask UnitY: stage 1 trains an X2T model (w2v-BERT 2.0 Conformer speech encoder + length adaptor + NLLB-derived text encoder/decoder) on X-eng S2TT and English ASR; stage 2 adds eng-X S2TT and non-English ASR; stage 3 freezes X2T and fine-tunes a 6+6 layer text-to-unit model on 121K hours of S2ST data, with a multilingual HiFi-GAN unit vocoder. Training data mix human-labeled, NLLB-pseudo-labeled and mined (SeamlessAlign) data.

datasets.name: Raw audio for mining
datasets.size: 4 million hours, about 1 million hours English
datasets.source: publicly available repository of crawled web data
datasets.preprocessing: URL dedup, resample to 16 kHz, audio event detection to drop non-speech, Silero VAD splitting, LID, over-segmentation (about 8x segments)

datasets.name: SeamlessAlign
datasets.size: about 470,000 h over 37 languages (Sen2Txx about 200,000 h; Sxx2Ten about 240,000 h; Sxx2Sen about 29,000 h); metadata released up to Sonar threshold 1.15
datasets.source: mined with Sonar embeddings and FAISS, margin criterion k=16, threshold 1.15
datasets.preprocessing: top 400 h per X-eng direction (33 directions) and top 200 h per eng-X direction (29 directions) of S2TT used, +18.3K h; up to 2,500 h per direction of S2ST

datasets.name: X2T supervised data (ASR + S2TT)
datasets.size: Table 38 totals (garbled in extraction): ASR primary 40,012 h; X-eng S2TT 50,596 h primary and 12,682 h mined; eng-X mined 5,701 h
datasets.source: human-labeled open-source and licensed data plus pseudo-labeled ASR (NLLB-200-3.3B translating ASR transcripts)
datasets.preprocessing: drop special tokens, max 100 sub-word tokens, skewed text/audio ratio over 5 sub-words per second removed; toxicity imbalance threshold 1; audio 0.1 s to 50 s; text over 250 sub-words, over 20% emojis, over 50% punctuation or spaces removed

datasets.name: S2ST data
datasets.size: 121K h total (Table 39 totals 26,254 + 23,171 + 49,425 + 21,983 h: X-eng primary, X-eng mined, eng-X primary, eng-X mined)
datasets.source: primary pseudo-labeled via a multilingual T2U model, plus mined SeamlessAlign S2ST with in-house ASR for first-pass text
datasets.preprocessing: pairs with audio seconds per text token above 0.5 discarded; unit extraction with XLS-R-1B layer 35, k-means K=10000

datasets.name: T2TT bitext
datasets.size: NLLB-200 data limited to 95 languages plus over 75M extra bitexts (arb, cmn, fra, rus, spa)
datasets.source: NLLB data plus open-source T2TT sets

datasets.name: LID training data
datasets.size: 17k h, average 171 h per language, 1 to 600 h

datasets.name: Fleurs
datasets.size: 102 languages, up to 350 test sentences, up to 3 speakers each

datasets.name: CVSS-C
datasets.size: 21 languages into English; 8 languages have missing samples

datasets.name: HolisticBias and Multilingual HolisticBias
datasets.size: 472K English sentences; speech extension 325 sentences over 19 languages
datasets.source: Smith et al. 2022; Costa-jussa et al. 2023
datasets.preprocessing: numbers converted to words, synthesized with MMS-TTS; English side with fairseq S^2 transformer-tts

models.name: SeamlessM4T-Large
models.architecture: multitask UnitY: Conformer speech encoder, Transformer text encoder/decoder, Transformer T2U, HiFi-GAN vocoder
models.init_from: w2v-BERT 2.0 (669M incl. length adaptor), SeamlessM4T-NLLB-1.3B (1,370M), pre-trained T2U (287M)
models.tokenizer: SentencePiece BPE retrained on NLLB data, forced inclusion of top 5000 Chinese/kanji characters seen at least 15 times
models.layers: w2v-BERT 2.0: 24 Conformer layers; T2U: 6 encoder + 6 decoder

other.length_adaptor: modified M-adaptor with one shared pooling module for Q, K, V
other.hifigan: multilingual, 36 target languages, language embedding, LID auxiliary loss, embedding dim 1280 for duration predictor and LID classifier

models.name: SeamlessM4T-NLLB-1.3B
models.architecture: dense NLLB 1.3B T2TT trained on 95 languages

models.name: w2v-BERT 2.0
models.architecture: contrastive + masked prediction, product quantization with 2 GVQ codebooks, plus RPQ masked prediction

other.loss: L = wc*Lc + wmGVQ*LmGVQ + wmRPQ*LmRPQ with weights 1.0, 0.5, 0.5

models.name: Sonar
models.architecture: NLLB-1.3B encoder-decoder with mean-pooled fixed-size bottleneck; speech encoders: w2v-BERT 2.0 + 3-layer seq2seq attention pooling, MSE loss to text embeddings

other.speech_encoders: trained on human ASR transcripts only, at least 100 h for most languages, languages grouped by family

other.note: external results copied from their papers with matched scoring

models.name: Blaser 2.0
models.architecture: 3-layer perceptron with tanh on 6 concatenated Sonar-derived vectors

other.training: 50% dropout, weight decay 0.1, batch size 1024, linear LR decay to zero, 50 epochs

training.objective: L = alpha*L_S2TT + beta*L_T2TT + gamma*L_KD (alpha, beta, gamma tuned on dev, values not given); L_KD is token-level KL from T2TT teacher to S2TT student; auto-encoding teacher for ASR data. Stage 3: only T2U fine-tuned on S2ST data, X2T frozen. Text decoder in S2TT ablation trained with LNA-D.

other.final_model_hyperparameters: The paper gives no learning rate, batch size, steps, optimizer, hardware or compute for the final stage 1-3 training, or for w2v-BERT 2.0 pre-training.
other.w2v_bert_ablation (Sec 4.5.1): LR up to 3e-4 over 4000 warm-up updates then inverse square root; 32 GPUs; batch of 960K frames per GPU; 100K updates; all speech encoder parameters trained, text decoder LayerNorm and self-attention only (LNA-D)
other.multitask_ablation (Sec 4.5.2): 100K updates (5-7 epochs); LayerDrop p=0.1 with masking p=0.1 on speech encoder; dropout p=0.1 on text encoder-decoder; LNA; last checkpoint evaluated
other.s2st_ablation: 50K and 80K updates equal 2 epochs in two data settings (Table 25)
other.stages: Stage1 X-eng S2TT + English ASR (found necessary for both X-eng and eng-X quality); Stage2 adds eng-X S2TT and non-English ASR; Stage3 S2ST 121K h
other.T2U: 12+12 layer T2U used for pseudo-labeling, 6+6 layer T2U distilled with its labels for UnitY
other.unit_extraction: XLS-R-1B layer 35, 50 Hz, 10K samples per language for k-means, K in {1000,2000,5000,10000}, K=10000 best

inference.decoding: beam search width 5 for text; two-pass beam search for S2ST and T2ST with beam 5 in both passes; beam 10 for S2TT in the bias study
inference.samples: single deterministic decode; bias experiments repeated 3 times because MMS-TTS is non-deterministic

other.ASR_scorer: Whisper-Medium for X-eng and Whisper-Large-v2 for eng-X ASR-BLEU

metrics.name: BLEU / spBLEU
metrics.definition: SacreBLEU (13a, or char tokenization for cmn, jpn, tha, lao, mya); spBLEU with Flores-200 sentencepiece

metrics.name: ASR-BLEU
metrics.definition: BLEU on Whisper transcripts of generated speech

metrics.name: Blaser 2.0
metrics.definition: similarity of Sonar embeddings of source, output and reference; supervised version predicts XSTS

metrics.name: XSTS
metrics.definition: human semantic similarity, 1-5, median of 3-5 annotators, calibrated

metrics.name: chrFMS / CoefVarMS
metrics.definition: mean and coefficient of variation of chrF across speakers reading the same content

metrics.name: ETOX / ASR-ETOX
metrics.definition: added toxicity: output has more word-list toxic items than input

eval.protocol: Automatic metrics on a single run; no seeds or significance tests reported for translation scores. Human XSTS: up to 30 annotators per pair, 3 per item, 2 more when scores differ by 2 or more, 500-item cross-lingual calibration set, bootstrap CI about plus or minus 0.1.

availability.data: metadata to recreate unfiltered 470,000 h SeamlessAlign; training audio not released

limits: Final-model training hyperparameters, hardware, compute and seeds are not reported; only ablation settings are given.
Model card: research model, not for production; not intended for long-form translation (trained on short inputs); not for domain-specific use such as medical or legal.
S2ST human XSTS is below the cascade for X-eng and the authors link this to truncation and omission in long inputs (falls off above about 8 s) and to many 'audio issues'.

Human evaluation covers 24 high and mid resource languages with at most 2 speakers per sentence, 3 annotators per item, and single-annotator MOS for 14 languages with no calibration; human results are called preliminary.
Toxicity and gender-representation checks use word lists and string matching (over-detection, tokenization errors, ASR false negatives); Fleurs detections are 81-84% false positives.
Mining covers 37 languages only; Sen2Txx and other directions left for future work; only top-scored subsets of SeamlessAlign used in training.
Quality gap: SeamlessM4T-Large lags AudioPaLM by 3.7 BLEU on CoVoST 2 X-eng and trails MMS variants using n-gram LMs by 5% WER on Fleurs-54; larger cascades beat it on eng-X S2TT.
Expressivity, prosody and streaming/low-latency translation are not addressed.
Gender bias: about 10% masculine preference when gender is unspecified and about 3% lower quality on feminine source speech; comparable to baselines, not mitigated.
Several numbers are inconsistent within the paper (CVSS gain 58% / 50% / 14 points; noise and speaker robustness 38% / 49% in abstract versus 33.3% / 42.2% and 49.4% in body).
